segments.ch01.s0010: Alice sat by the river with her big sister.
segments.ch01.s0020: Her sister was reading a thick book.
segments.ch01.s0030: The book had no pictures in it.
segments.ch01.s0050: What is the good of a book like that?
segments.ch01.s0060: The day was hot, and Alice felt sleepy.
segments.ch01.s0070: She thought about making a daisy chain.
segments.ch01.s0080: But picking the flowers felt like too much work.
segments.ch01.s0090: Just then a white rabbit ran past her.
segments.ch01.s0110: Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!
segments.ch01.s0120: Alice did not think that was very strange.
segments.ch01.s0130: Then the rabbit took a watch out of his coat pocket.
segments.ch01.s0140: He looked at the time and hurried on.
segments.ch01.s0150: Alice jumped up onto her feet.
segments.ch01.s0160: She had never seen a rabbit with a pocket.
segments.ch01.s0170: She had never seen a rabbit with a watch.
segments.ch01.s0180: Alice ran after him across the field.
segments.ch01.s0190: She saw him pop down a big hole under the hedge.
segments.ch01.s0210: She never once thought about getting out again.
segments.ch01.s0220: The hole ran straight ahead, like a tunnel.
segments.ch01.s0230: Then it dropped away under her feet.
segments.ch01.s0240: Alice was falling down a deep, deep well.
segments.ch01.s0250: Maybe the well was very deep.
segments.ch01.s0260: Maybe she was falling very slowly.
segments.ch01.s0270: Either way, she had plenty of time to look around.
segments.ch01.s0280: She looked down, but it was too dark to see.
segments.ch01.s0290: The walls were full of cupboards and shelves.
segments.ch01.s0300: Maps and pictures hung on little pegs.
segments.ch01.s0310: Alice took a jar off a shelf as she passed.
segments.ch01.s0340: She did not drop it, in case somebody was below.
segments.ch01.s0350: So she tucked it into a cupboard as she fell past.
segments.ch01.s0360: After a fall like this, stairs will be nothing!
segments.ch01.s0370: Everyone at home will think I am very brave.
segments.ch01.s0390: Would the fall never come to an end?
segments.ch01.s0400: How many miles have I fallen now?
segments.ch01.s0410: I must be near the middle of the earth.
segments.ch01.s0420: That would be four thousand miles down.
segments.ch01.s0430: There was nobody down there to listen.
segments.ch01.s0440: But saying it out loud was good practice.
segments.ch01.s0450: What if I fall right through the earth?
segments.ch01.s0460: Then I will come out where people walk upside down.
segments.ch01.s0470: I will have to ask them the name of the country.
segments.ch01.s0480: She tried a polite little bow as she fell.
segments.ch01.s0490: Can you imagine bowing in the middle of the air?
segments.ch01.s0500: Still she fell. Down, down, down.
segments.ch01.s0510: Dinah will miss me very much tonight.
segments.ch01.s0530: I hope they remember her milk at teatime.
segments.ch01.s0540: Dinah, dear, I wish you were down here with me.
segments.ch01.s0550: There are no mice in the air, I am afraid.
segments.ch01.s0560: But you might catch a bat instead.
segments.ch01.s0570: A bat is very like a mouse, you know.
segments.ch01.s0600: She could not answer either question.
segments.ch01.s0610: Alice was growing very sleepy now.
segments.ch01.s0620: She began to dream of walking hand in hand with Dinah.
segments.ch01.s0640: Alice landed on a heap of sticks and dry leaves.
segments.ch01.s0660: She was not hurt at all, and jumped straight up.
segments.ch01.s0680: In front of her ran another long passage.
segments.ch01.s0690: The white rabbit was still hurrying down it.
segments.ch01.s0700: Away went Alice, as fast as the wind.
segments.ch01.s0710: Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it is getting!
segments.ch01.s0720: The rabbit said it as he turned a corner.
segments.ch01.s0730: Alice turned the corner too, but he was gone.
segments.ch01.s0740: She was standing in a long, low hall.
segments.ch01.s0750: A row of lamps hung from the ceiling.
segments.ch01.s0760: Doors stood all around the hall.
segments.ch01.s0790: She walked sadly down the middle of the hall.
segments.ch01.s0800: Then she found a little table made of glass.
segments.ch01.s0810: On it lay one tiny golden key.
segments.ch01.s0820: But the key was too small for every lock.
segments.ch01.s0830: On her second time round, she saw a low curtain.
segments.ch01.s0840: Behind the curtain was a little door.
segments.ch01.s0850: It was no taller than her arm.
segments.ch01.s0860: The little golden key fitted it perfectly.
segments.ch01.s0870: Alice opened the door and knelt down.
segments.ch01.s0880: Beyond it was a passage no wider than a rat hole.
segments.ch01.s0890: At the far end lay the loveliest garden.
segments.ch01.s0900: Bright flowers grew there, and cool fountains played.
segments.ch01.s0910: But Alice could not even fit her head through.
segments.ch01.s0920: I wish I could fold up small, like a telescope.
segments.ch01.s0930: So many strange things had happened today.
segments.ch01.s0940: Alice was starting to think almost nothing was impossible.
segments.ch01.s0950: She went back to the glass table.
segments.ch01.s0960: Now a little bottle stood on it.
segments.ch01.s0970: That was certainly not here before.
segments.ch01.s0980: A paper label hung round its neck.
segments.ch01.s0990: The label said DRINK ME in big letters.
segments.ch01.s1000: Clever Alice did not drink it right away.
segments.ch01.s1010: First I will look for the word poison.
segments.ch01.s1020: That word was nowhere on the bottle.
segments.ch01.s1030: So Alice took one tiny taste.
segments.ch01.s1040: It tasted of cherry pie, custard and hot buttered toast.
segments.ch01.s1050: Alice soon drank the whole bottle.
segments.ch01.s1070: I am folding up like a telescope.
segments.ch01.s1090: Now Alice was only ten inches tall.
segments.ch01.s1100: At last she was the right size for the little door.
segments.ch01.s1110: She waited, in case she grew smaller still.
segments.ch01.s1120: It might end with me going out, like a candle.
segments.ch01.s1130: Nothing more happened, so off she went to the garden.
segments.ch01.s1150: She had left the little golden key on the table.
segments.ch01.s1160: She could see it through the glass top.
segments.ch01.s1170: She tried to climb a table leg, but it was too slippery.
segments.ch01.s1190: There is no use crying like that.
segments.ch01.s1210: She gave herself very good advice.
segments.ch01.s1230: Then she saw a little glass box under the table.
segments.ch01.s1240: Inside was a very small cake.
segments.ch01.s1250: The words EAT ME were marked on it in currants.
segments.ch01.s1270: If I grow bigger, I can reach the key.
segments.ch01.s1280: If I grow smaller, I can creep under the door.
segments.ch01.s1290: Either way, I get into the garden!
segments.ch01.s1320: She put a hand on her head to feel which way she grew.
segments.ch01.s1340: She stayed exactly the same size.
segments.ch01.s1350: That is what usually happens when you eat cake.
segments.ch01.s1360: But Alice now expected strange things.
segments.ch01.s1370: So she set to work and finished the whole cake.
